text: Find 3 things at home you could reuse instead of buying new.
I have a head and a tail but no body. What am I?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Think of something in your pocket that jingles.

text: Put one coin in your piggy bank today, even a small one.
You have 50p and buy a sweet for 30p. How much change do you get?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Take 30 away from 50 and try again.

text: Before asking for something, wait one whole day. Do you still want it?
What gets bigger the more you save it?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Think about what grows when you add coins to it.

text: Draw a picture of something you are saving up for.
Which is worth more: three 10p coins or one 20p coin?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Add up the three 10p coins and compare.

text: Switch off lights in empty rooms today to save energy.
I'm made of paper, I'm worth more than a coin, and the King is on me. What am I?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Coins are metal. What money is made of paper?

text: Make a 'need or want' list of 5 things. Which are needs?
If you save 10p every day for a week, how much will you have?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! There are 7 days in a week. Count 10p seven times.

text: Play shop with a grown-up and practise giving change.
What has many pennies but can't buy anything?
answer: A piggy bank... until you open it!
choices: A piggy bank... until you open it!
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Think of something that holds pennies but never goes shopping.

text: Share something today: a snack, a toy or some of your time.
A comic costs £2. You have £1.20. How much more do you need?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Count up from £1.20 to £2.

text: Make a savings jar label with your goal written on it.
Which two UK coins have 7 sides?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Have a look at the coins with flat edges.

text: Fix or tidy something instead of throwing it away.
You split £1 equally with a friend. How much do you each get?
Count all the coins in your piggy bank. How much is there?
What do you call money you keep for later?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! It's what goes in your piggy bank for later.

text: Compare the price of two snacks at the shop. Which is better value?
How many 5p coins make £1?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Try counting in 5s up to 100.

text: Have a no-spend day: enjoy free fun like the park or drawing.
I'm round, I'm gold and silver, and I'm worth £2. What am I?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Look for the coin with two colours.

text: Think of one way you could help at home to earn a sticker or treat.
A toy costs £5. You save £1 a week. How many weeks until you can buy it?
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Add £1 each week until you reach £5.

text: Write a thank-you note for something someone gave you.
What's the difference between a need and a want?
answer: A need is something you must have; a want is nice to have
choices: A need is something you must have; a want is nice to have
A want is always more expensive
feedback_wrong: Not quite! Think about food (a need) and a new toy (a want).
